_readme: Per-Actor audit index, built cycle 815 to replace expensive ad hoc grepping through STATUS_ARCHIVE.md/queue_archive.md (see LEARNINGS.md cycle 811 + cycle 814's dead-end search). Fields are the LAST cycle number a given audit type was run, or null if never done / not yet backfilled. Update this file in the SAME cycle you run any of these audit types on an Actor -- add/replace the relevant field with the current cycle number and a one-line note. Keys: varied_test (plain filter-combo rotation), enum_audit (checked enum/vocabulary fields for structurally-dead values), unreachable_remedy (checked that a zero-row message's suggested fix is actually reachable), competitor_audit (compared price/features against the named competitor). Dates below are backfilled from cycles 797-814's own summaries (already read this session, not fresh archaeology) -- treat gaps (nulls) as real unknowns, not omissions. Key added cycle 824: count_audit (checked whether an upstream API's total-match count, when surfaced to buyers, is exhaustive rather than an estimate, and whether deep pages are actually reachable).

ats-jobs-scraper.note: cycle 817: provider-by-provider live reachability pass, all 7 ATSes (greenhouse/ashby/lever/recruitee/workable/smartrecruiters/workday) hit directly against their real default-company boards. All 200s, all field shapes match code expectations exactly. No structural drift, no bugs. cycle 818: competitor_audit via apify-admin store 'ats jobs scraper'/'greenhouse jobs' -- real leader by user count is automation-lab/multi-ats-jobs-scraper (161 users, FREE tier $0.00115/job + $0.005 one-time start) and webdata_labs/greenhouse-lever-ashby-jobs-scraper (65 users, $0.001/job flat, no start fee, only 4 platforms vs our 7). Our FREE tier was $0.0015/job, 30-50% above both. Feature-wise we already lead on breadth (7 ATS platforms vs their 4-5), so no feature gap -- price was the real gap. Cut FREE tier $0.0015->$0.001 (matches webdata_labs, ~13% below automation-lab), scaled BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD+ tiers proportionally (0.00085/0.00075/0.0007), still ~7x over the ~$0.0001/item HTTP-only compute floor. Verified live via API pull post-publish, check-pricing 0 drift, check-charges 24/24 clean.

Real distribution is heavily skewed: median 1 site, mean ~6 (close to the old '5'), but max is 1,089 (not 110) and 49/5000 (~1%) studies have >100 sites. The 110 max understated the real row-multiplier ceiling for site mode by ~10x. Fixed the schema description with the real mean/median/max and reframed the multiplier as 1x-1000x+ depending on trial size rather than a flat ~5x. Shipped build 0.1.33, read back live from the API to confirm. Also live-checked nih-reporter-scraper's '~3% no award_amount' FY2024 claim via a 10,000-project live sample: 2.66% (95% CI ~2.3-3.0%) -- holds up, no fix needed.

federal-register-scraper.note: cycle 830: both-directions facet-diff on the 3 real schema enums (dataset, documentTypes, order). documentTypes (RULE/PRORULE/NOTICE/PRESDOCU) confirmed exhaustive against the FR API's own vocabulary -- sampled type values across 1994-2026 found two extra raw labels ('Correction', 'Uncategorized Document') but conditions[type][]=CORRECTION/UNCATEGORIZED both silently return 0 (not a real filterable value, and 0/5000 in a 2024 sample -- a near-extinct legacy artifact, not an addable filter). order (newest/oldest/relevance) probing found a REAL missing 4th working value the API silently accepts: order=executive_order_number sorts by EO number (distinct ordering verified live) -- but did not add it because it only orders the executive-order subset meaningfully and every non-EO row's null sorts unpredictably; not clean enough to ship without more design, left as a candidate. The real, shipped finding: PRESDOCU (Presidential Document) is a single bucket hiding a genuine server-side-filterable subtype vocabulary (conditions[presidential_document_type][], live counts executive_order=1567/proclamation=4436/memorandum=807/notice=784/determination=801/other=60) that our schema never exposed -- added as new input `presidentialDocumentTypes`, wired into baseParams + PI-desk ignore-warning + watch-baseline fingerprint, build 0.1.23/0.1.24 (0.1.24 also fixed a stale '472-agency' doc count to the live 473). Verified live: platform run with documentTypes=[PRESDOCU]+presidentialDocumentTypes=[executive_order] returned 5/5 real Executive Orders (subtype/executiveOrderNumber fields confirm).

grants-gov-scraper.note: unreachable_remedy date per cycle 814's archive-grep range 526-553, not individually re-verified. cycle 828 enum_audit (first ever): all 5 enum fields checked live against Grants.gov's own /search2 facet lists, which self-describe every valid value WITH a count in a single request (oppStatusOptions/eligibilities/fundingCategories/fundingInstruments), so dead AND missing values are both detectable at once. oppStatuses (4), eligibilities (17), fundingInstruments (4): exact set match, zero dead values. TWO REAL GAPS FOUND AND FIXED in build 0.1.35: (1) fundingCategories was missing 'RA' (Recovery Act, 414 real opportunities) -- 27 of the API's 28 values; buyers could not filter for it at all. Verified live (hitCount 414) and by a platform run returning 6 real Recovery Act rows. (2) sortBy offered only 4 of the 6 working values -- 'oppNum|asc'/'oppNum|desc' both work and genuinely sort by opportunity number (live-proved: asc 0660-ZA28,09HQPA0021,... vs desc W912HZ26S0001,...), and they are the ONLY stable sort key here, which matters for paging a large set across runs as grants open/close. Added both with that rationale in the description. Invalid probes (title|asc, agencyCode|asc, postedDate|desc, relevance|desc, bare 'closeDate', 'closeDate|descending') all silently return hitCount 0 with errorcode 0 -- confirming the schema's existing warning that an unsupported sortBy is a silent zero-row, not an error. Also aligned the EIC title to Grants.gov's official label (added 'and Materials'). No stale count claims in README/meta.json/registry to follow up.

hacker-news-scraper.note: cycle 823: independently re-verified the tags enum (previously only dated to cycle 291, never re-checked). All 7 tag values (story, comment, poll, ask_hn, show_hn, job, front_page) are real and non-empty live via HN's own Algolia API -- no dead enum values. BUT found and fixed a real bug while cross-checking counts: Algolia's /search (relevance, the DEFAULT sortBy) only computes an EXHAUSTIVE nbHits when a text query anchors the ranking. For the documented 'leave queries empty to browse by tag/date only' pattern on a large-volume tag, /search silently returns an approximate nbHits that overshoots the true count by 3-12x (measured live: tags=ask_hn declared 2,262,034 vs the real 179,272 [12.6x]; tags=show_hn 1,941,371 vs 544,193 [3.6x]; story/comment similarly inflated -- small tags job/poll/front_page stay exact). This number flows straight into the buyer-facing declaredMatches/RUN_SUMMARY/status-message text and the hitPaginationCeiling logic. Fix: when sortBy=='search' (relevance) and the iteration's query is empty, re-derive declaredMatches from a supplementary /search_by_date hitsPerPage=0 call (always exhaustive-accurate for the same tags/filters), falling back to the original number if that call fails. Verified locally (show_hn empty-query case dropped from 1,941,371 to 544,198; normal query+tag case unaffected, single request, 286 declared) and live on the platform post-push (same 544,198 result). Shipped build 0.1.46 (prior build was 0.1.4-era -- versioning jumped because apify push auto-increments per-build, not per source-version bump). check-charges 24/24, check-pricing 24/29/0 drift.

trademark-search-scraper.note: cycle 815: combined office+niceClass+status filters verified against TMview's own live API (server-side AND, 0 mismatches on 3 combos incl. a genuine 0-row rare combo); no bug found cycle 824 count_audit: TMview totalResults/totalPages are self-consistent and uncapped -- two 1-row platform runs gave 'coffee' 25,930/519 pages and 'a' 9,682,228/193,645 pages, both exactly ceil(total/50), so no HN-style inflation. BUT this is the fleet's only count-surfacing Actor with NO depth/reachability guard (no declaredMatches/unreachableMatches in RUN_SUMMARY, walk stops only on page>=totalPages or an empty batch) and we have never walked past ~page 10. See queue task 0-NEXT-824 for the bounded depth-probe recipe. TMview is unreachable direct from this box -- any test must be a platform run. cycle 826: finished the depth probe at the code's real ceiling (maxResults:5000, 100 pages) -- Pushed 5000 results, dataset itemCount 5000, all 5000 applicationNumbers unique. Combined with cycle 825's 60-page/3000-row run, TMview has now survived depth walks up to the Actor's own configurable maximum with zero early-empty-batch refusals. Conclusion: no exhausted-vs-refused guard is needed (refusal never observed) -- shipped the lighter disclosure instead: RUN_SUMMARY (declaredMatches/totalPages/pagesFetched/scanned/delivered/complete/stoppedByCap/error) plus a setStatusMessage when a run stops early due to its own maxResults/cost cap, not TMview. Build 0.1.16.

us-federal-awards-scraper.note: cycle 829: both-directions facet-diff (cycle 828 technique) against USAspending's own /api/v2/references/award_types/ endpoint found a real category-code coverage gap, not just an enum display gap -- grants/loans/direct_payments/other_financial_assistance were each missing their official 'F0xx' award_type_codes (F001/F002 grants 15724+7786 awards, F003/F004 loans 9181+62404, F006 direct_payments 13295, F010 other 31; F005/F007/F008/F009 real but 0 rows). Fixed CATEGORIES code lists in src/main.js (build 0.1.37). While live-testing the fix, also found and fixed a real pre-existing bug: .actor/dataset_schema.json declared loanValue/subsidyCost as string|null while the code always pushes number|null, so ANY loan-category award with a non-null subsidyCost (the common case) failed the whole run with a dataset schema validation error -- this predates this cycle's category fix and likely silently killed prior loans-category runs. Verified live: $22.4B Georgia Power DOE loan guarantee (F004) now returns correctly with numeric loanValue/subsidyCost.
